source_inspiration.pathforge_fit_adaptation: The outside need is composing rich travel/poster image prompts. This package does not call any image generator; it adapts that demand into an offline stamp-layout game/editor where users arrange landmark, texture, type, and sticker tiles, receive composition-goal feedback, and export a concise poster brief.

verification_notes: Static scan of final artifact found no http/https URLs, script src, linked hrefs, @import, fetch/XMLHttpRequest/WebSocket/EventSource, unsafe dynamic HTML sinks, inline event attributes, or negative letter-spacing.
Final artifact contains one inline script and it parsed with new Function().

Chrome local HTTP render on http://127.0.0.1:8794/public/artifacts/travel-poster-layout-stamp-game-gemini.html was nonblank with Poster Tools, all four Add controls, Reset Board, Copy Poster Brief, and poster board present.
Interaction check added landmark, texture, typography, and sticker stamps; score reached 70/100 with diversity and balance feedback.
Drag check moved the typography stamp upward; score updated to 100/100 with Strong headline placement feedback.
Copy/export check wrote a poster brief to the system clipboard with final score 100/100 and stamp coordinates; export button changed to Copied.
Reset check removed all stamps and returned feedback to Score: 0/100 / Add elements to begin composing.
Chrome console warning/error log was empty during interaction verification.
Headless Chrome at 390x900 loaded the final artifact and the dumped DOM showed the responsive branch active with poster board transform scale(0.91); no full screenshot was captured.

steps.prompt_exact: Build me a playful offline browser game/editor where I arrange landmark, texture, type, and sticker stamps on a travel poster board, get scored on composition goals, and can reset or copy a concise poster brief from the final layout as a single saveable HTML file.
steps.response_summary: Initial canvas version added random colored blocks and count-based scoring, but did not support drag/repositioning or type stamps and used inline onclick handlers.
code_blocks:
Stamp Box

Add Landmark
Add Texture
Add Sticker
Score: 0
steps.notes: Rejected as final because it lacked core drag/drop placement, type/headline stamp, composition-goal scoring, and used inline onclick handlers.

steps.prompt_exact: This version is not usable yet: the stamps only appear randomly, I cannot drag or reposition them on the poster, there is no type/headline stamp, the score is just item count, and the HTML uses inline onclick handlers. Please replace it with a complete single-file version where users can place and move landmark, texture, type, and sticker tiles on the poster, earn composition-goal feedback, reset, and copy a poster brief without inline event attributes or unsafe dynamic HTML.
steps.response_summary: Drag/drop DOM version added the missing interaction and better scoring but still used feedbackPanel.innerHTML and board.innerHTML.
code_blocks:
Poster Tools

Score: 0
Add elements to begin composing.
steps.continuation_reason: V1 lacked drag/repositioning, type/headline stamp, useful composition goals, and used inline onclick handlers.
steps.notes: Rejected as final because static inspection found unsafe dynamic HTML sinks: feedbackPanel.innerHTML and board.innerHTML.

steps.prompt_exact: The drag version is much closer, but it still uses innerHTML for feedback and reset, which will fail my safety check. Please return the full single-file HTML again with the same drag/drop poster game, but remove every innerHTML/outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML/document.write use; build feedback with textContent and DOM nodes, reset with replaceChildren, and keep the copy/export brief working.
steps.response_summary: Safety repair removed unsafe dynamic HTML sinks, but the fixed-width desktop layout would clip narrow viewports.
code_blocks: Poster Tools
steps.continuation_reason: V2 still used innerHTML for feedback and reset, which would fail the safety gate.
steps.notes: Rejected as final because fixed 280px sidebar plus fixed 500px board with hidden overflow would break narrow rendering.

steps.prompt_exact: One more issue: this will clip on a narrow screen because the sidebar plus fixed 500px board are wider than the viewport and body hides overflow. Please return the full single-file HTML again with the same stamp game and no unsafe dynamic HTML sinks, but make the layout responsive: desktop/tablet can stay two-column, while narrow screens stack the tools above a scaled poster board with no horizontal clipping.
steps.response_summary: Final responsive pointer-event version passed static safety and local interaction verification.
code_blocks: Poster Tools
steps.continuation_reason: V3 would clip on narrow screens because the sidebar plus fixed board exceeded the viewport and body hid overflow.
